external_entities.name: Shoppers
external_entities.description: People who browse the storefront and place orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders; it receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: It is not exposed outside. Its database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service reads and writes it with a single application account that has full read/write.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders, including which order was written and that the order service wrote it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: browse and place orders
data_flows.description: Shoppers browse the storefront and submit orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.authentication: email and password with a session cookie

data_flows.name: submit orders
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC
data_flows.notes: There is no authentication on the gRPC call; the order service accepts anything that can reach it.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_flows.name: write receipts
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: Completed-order receipts recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: payment webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment to tell the system the order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone containing shoppers and the storefront API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal network containing the order service and orders database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud Storage
trust_boundaries.description: The Cloud Storage hosting zone containing the receipt archive.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

assumptions.assumption: The orders-db data is confidential because it contains shopper addresses and card-last-four data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db contains shopper addresses and card-last-four data, which are personal and payment-related records.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is in a separate tenant-controlled Cloud Storage zone.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the receipt archive as a Cloud Storage bucket; Cloud Storage is treated as a separately controlled hosting zone.
